prime.problem: One chain of thought can slip at any step, and greedy decoding gives you exactly one chain, the same one every time. You get no second opinion and no sign of how sure the model is.
prime.fits: Builds on chain-of-thought prompting (one written chain) and on sampling with temperature (why repeated runs differ). Here many sampled chains vote; the process-rewards card later replaces the vote with a trained grader.
prime.goal: Explain why voting over sampled chains beats one greedy chain, compute a vote and its agreement by hand, and say when voting can't help.

attend: Why does the vote need temperature above 0, when one sampled chain is less accurate than the greedy one?
What assumption about how chains go wrong makes counting final answers work?
Why did weighting each vote by the model's own probability barely change the result?
Why does beam search get worse as the beam widens while sampling gets better?
Which kinds of task make the vote impossible, and which make it pick the wrong answer?

must: Temperature > 0 → each chain takes a different route → slips land in different places → wrong answers scatter while right answers pile up → the most common answer is more often right
Greedy gives one chain → no comparison is possible → sampling N chains and voting adds evidence → GSM8K PaLM 540B 56.5% → 74.4% with 40 chains
Extra chains mostly confirm the leading answer → returns shrink fast → UL2-20B AQuA 19.7 / 24.9 / 25.3 / 26.7 / 26.9% at 1 / 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 chains → start with 5–10

The vote only reads final answers → needs answers from a fixed set and ignores the working → free text can't vote, and a lucky chain counts like a sound one → a trained step grader beats it at large N (78.2% vs 69.6%)
elevated: Beam search keeps the most likely chains → near copies with low diversity → its top chain drops 23.6% → 10.2% as beams grow, and a vote over beams trails a vote over samples (24.2% vs 26.9%)
The model rates its chains as about equally likely → weighting votes by probability adds nothing (74.1% vs 74.4%) → plain counting is enough
reference: Sampling settings: PaLM 540B T = 0.7, top-k 40; UL2-20B and LaMDA-137B T = 0.5, top-k 40; GPT-3 T = 0.7
Main results: 40 sampled chains, averaged over 10 runs, same 8 exemplars as the CoT paper
Other GSM8K gains: code-davinci-002 60.1% → 78.0%, LaMDA-137B 17.1% → 27.7%, UL2-20B 4.1% → 7.3%
Answer parsing: the number after 'The answer is'

compress.prompt: From memory, explain in 3–4 sentences why many sampled chains plus a vote beat one greedy chain, and why the gain levels off. Or redraw the ten-chain tally.
checklist: greedy is one deterministic chain; sampling gives varied chains
wrong chains rarely agree on the same wrong answer, right chains do
count final answers, keep the most common
returns shrink quickly as N grows (5–10 chains capture most of it)
needs comparable answers and costs N times the tokens

retrieve.q: Explain the assumption self-consistency makes about right and wrong reasoning chains, and why the vote depends on it.
answer: many different routes reach the one right answer
mistakes happen in different places and give different wrong answers
so the right answer is the most common one
if mistakes all agree, the vote picks the mistake

retrieve.q: Walk through self-consistency for one question, from the prompt to the returned answer.
answer: use the chain-of-thought prompt
sample N chains with temperature above 0
parse each chain's final answer
return the most common answer (agreement share is a confidence signal)

retrieve.q: You have a budget of 10× the tokens of one answer. Argue between 10 voted chains and one chain from a bigger model, and say what would change your mind.
answer: voting needs no new model and gave +18 points on GSM8K for PaLM 540B
a small model gains less from voting (UL2-20B +3.2)
free-text tasks can't vote, which favours the bigger model
measure: if chains already mostly agree, more votes won't help

compare.q: Both majority voting and a process reward model choose among N samples. What does each read, and why does the reward model pull ahead at large N?
answer: the vote reads only final answers and needs no extra model
the PRM reads and scores every step
the PRM can pick a correct minority answer the vote would discard
best-of-1,860 on MATH: PRM 78.2% vs vote 69.6%

compare.q: Chain of thought gives one model room to think; self-consistency gives it several tries. Which failure of chain of thought does voting fix, and which does it not?
answer: voting fixes scattered slips in one chain
it doesn't fix a model too small to do the steps
it doesn't make the steps faithful; lucky chains still count
it multiplies the token cost of chain of thought

predict.q: A model makes the same mistake on a question 70% of the time and gets it right 30% of the time. What happens to the vote's answer as you go from 1 to 40 sampled chains?
predict.answer: It gets more confidently wrong. With one chain you're right 30% of the time; with 40 chains the wrong answer almost always wins the count. Voting amplifies whatever the model does most often, so it only helps when the right answer is the most common one.

apply.task: Take the first five chains from the sketch (answers 18, 18, 26, 18, 14) and compute the vote and its agreement. Then do the same for all ten. Say whether the extra five chains changed the answer, and what changed instead.
apply.done: Five chains: $18 with 3 of 5 (60%). Ten chains: $18 with 6 of 10 (60%). The answer didn't change; you just spent twice the tokens to confirm it.
apply.hint: Agreement = votes for the winner ÷ number of chains.

reflect: Which prediction did you get wrong before reading: did you expect one sampled chain to beat greedy?
What couldn't you explain cleanly: why beams don't help, or why probability weighting adds nothing?
Which relationship is still fuzzy: temperature → varied chains, or varied chains → scattered wrong answers?
Which task in your own work has answers you could vote on, and which doesn't?
How would you decide N for a production system, given the plateau?
